newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Minicars hog limelight at Geneva.
newsitem.headline: Minicars hog limelight at Geneva.

text.p: Economy and value for money are the key themes of the Geneva car show, with minicars taking centre stage.
The SEAT Arosa will be the latest mini, or city car to emerge when it steps into the limelight at the annual show, which opens on Thursday and runs until March 16.

The Arosa is the first of a series of small cars from German mass car maker Volkswagen AG. VW owns SEAT, as well as the Audi and Skoda marques. The Arosa is the first SEAT product to be made in Germany.

France's Renault started this trend with the Twingo, followed last year by Ford's Ka. And to show that this isn't just for the cheap end of the market, Mercedes is demonstrating is sub-Fiesta sized "A" series here, although it will not be on sale until late this year.
"This is the first big salvo with these new, basic sector cars, said Peter Schmidt, joint managing director of Britain's Automotive Industry Data.

"The Arosa is based on the Polo (currently VW's smallest) and shows Volkswagen is re-entering the market it last led in the 1960s with the Beetle. VW is finally living up to its name; this is a wagon for the folks, an affordable car for the masses," Schmidt said.
Schmidt said the Arosa will be followed by a VW branded version, the Lupo, and next year will see an even cheaper version, the Lupino.
There are some more upmarket cars making their debuts in Geneva.

Audi will present its new A6 - a mid-size executive saloon competing with the BMW 5 series and Mercedes E class. Engines available include a 2.8 litre six cylinder, a 1.8 litre five cylinder, a 2.4 litre V6, and a 1.9 litre turbo diesel.
Ford will unveil its Puma coupe based on a Fiesta, which will compete with the Opel Tigra.

But it is the arrival of little, unpretentious cars that shows the current preoccupation of the European industry. And this is not without danger, because other moves into niche markets like the Multi Purpose Vehicle - luxury vans seating up to eight - have led to overproduction and profit margin pressures.

Arthur Maher, head of European forecasting at J.D.Power-LMC Automotive, said that in a generally stagnant market, manufacturers have spotted a niche market of the affluent who want second cars or "city" cars.
Maher says European manufacturers plan to raise production to about one million in five years, up from around 500,000 now.

"This is big numbers we are talking. This could be incremental volume for Mercedes, but poses real problems for the likes of Ford and VW. To what degree does this take sales from Fiesta and Polo? This product proliferation will make the market more competitive. This is good for the consumer but difficult for manufacturers," Maher said.
Karel Williams, director of graduate studies at Manchester University, also says this is a dangerous game for the car makers.

"The industry is making things worse for itself by pursuing extra volume with niche variants like the Tigra, Ka and Puma, and MPVs. These are all essentially variants and repackaging of existing mechanicals and move the industry further away from standardisation, " Williams said.

"With these endless niche models the industry is cannibalising its own sales. Models like the Ford Ka are not so clever; clearly to some extent they will divert from larger and more expensive/profitable cars," Williams said.

Other new models are thin on the ground at Geneva, but a couple of technological improvements might excite motoring afficianados. Mitsubishi is close to selling some of its Nedcar, Netherlands produced Carisma cars with direct injection petrol engines. These engines give diesel-like economy and petrol engine performance.
And Ford is leading the way with satellite based navigation devices. Some of its top of the range Mondeos will have this as an option.
The second big show of the year in Frankfurt in the autumn will have many more significant models.
Among new models in Framkfurt will be the VW Golf, the Opel Astra, BMW 3, Saab 9-5, Citroen ZX, Mazda 626, Honda Accord, and VW's new Beetle.
